svg.title: Tested is not proven. An energy app: customers send a photo of their electricity meter and an AI reads the number for their bill. A newer AI model passed all 1,200 test photos and went to every customer on Monday; none of the photos showed an older meter with a red last digit, so it read 4,512.7 as 45,127. By Thursday, 6,000 wrong bills, 1,900 paid by direct debit. Sent to 5% first with a stop rule, it switched back at noon on Monday and 0 wrong bills went out.
svg.desc: Top row, red: a customer photographs a meter showing 04512 and a red 7; a developer switches the reading to a newer AI model for everyone on Monday after it passed 1,200 test photos; the AI reads 4,512.7 as 45,127, and by Thursday 6,000 customers have wrong bills and 1,900 have paid by direct debit. Strip: none of the test photos showed a red last digit, and nobody noticed for three days. Bottom row, green: the same change goes to 5% of photos, picked at random, with a stop rule written before it starts; at the noon check, readings more than 3 times the home's usual use are 24 of 250 on the new model against 19 of 4,750 on the old one; it switches back by itself, the 24 photos are read again, and 0 wrong bills go out. Strip: everyone at once, 6,000 wrong bills; 5% first, 0. Footer: let a few real users meet the change before everyone does.
